Home
Homeowners experiencing well interference must pay out-of-pocket for temporary water supplies and well driller inspections while investigations take place

If a commercial cone of depression overlaps with nearby shallow domestic wells or city water supply wells, water levels can drop below the intake pumps of local homes. Under Minnesota Rules 6115.0730, heavy appropriators can be held liable for causing well interference, but investigating these failures after the fact forces local homeowners to rely on temporary emergency water supplies while lengthy state investigations take place.
If unmeasured, a severe cone of depression causes “well interference,” leaving nearby home wells sucking dry air
In Minnesota, municipalities obtain water appropriation permits from the DNR to supply residential homes, small businesses, and essential services
